## BOOK 1 of 2: TOMMY (Joseph Hocking, 1916; Gutenberg 24986)
Front matter: title page "TOMMY, by Joseph Hocking, author of 'All for a Scrap of Paper', 'Dearer Than Life'; Hodder and Stoughton, London/New York/Toronto, MCMXVI". Other-stories list. NOTE by author: he addressed recruiting meetings, trained with soldiers, visited France/Flanders (La Bassee, Neuve Chapelle, Ypres); nearly every incident told by "Tommy" himself; signed "Priors' Corner, Totteridge, Herts, February 1916."

### Ch I (Sunday, first Sunday June 1914, Brunford, Lancashire cotton town)
- Tom Pollard leaves home in Dixon Street ~3:30 (Town Hall clock) for Thorn and Thistle pub (landlord Enoch Powell).
- Polly Powell (~24, buxom, bold-eyed, red-cheeked, highly coloured dresses, feathers) meets him; jealous of Alice Lister; mentions Jim Scott, Jim Dixon; says father says Tom has brains (3 prizes at Mechanics' Institute), would back him to start a mill. Tom says he has an appointment.
- Tom's background: parents weavers (father 30s/week; mother left mill); he expects Tackler's job; had dropped Sunday School; frequent Thorn and Thistle visitor.
- Alice Lister (~20, refined, contralto singer, pianist, French/German classes, daughter of small manufacturer who was once a weaver; educated, never worked at mill). Girls tease Tom (Emily Bilson, "Bull and Butcher landlord's son"). Alice walks with Tom up Liverpool Road into Scott's Park; ultimatum: choose her or Thorn and Thistle/Polly. Tom mentions Harry Briarfield at Alice's supper. Alice: "Duty, God." Tom says "I would rather have you than forty Polly Powells" but chooses Waterman.
- Harry Waterman (tall, handsome, florid, light-brown hair; claims squire's son from Warwickshire; educated in English public school + German university; anti-religion; anti-German-sympathising-English-hater; Tom's "superior"); invites Tom to club at Rose and Crown. Tom chooses Polly; Alice: "I see you have made your choice." Alice leaves: "Good-bye, Tom."
- Polly takes Tom to tea. Mother Martha Pollard scolds that night ("brazen-faaced 'uzzy"; "Bein' fools runs in the family").

### Ch II (June 1914 onward)
- Brunford: boom in cotton trade; Tom drinks more, neglects studies; "Thorn and Thistle" habit; Jim Parkin reported he spent 4 shillings there.
- War: Austria/Serbia, Sir Edward Grey; manufacturers' talk about Germans; Enoch Powell predicts six weeks.
- Waterman says English fools, Germans will win; leaves.
- Mr. Shweitzer (German businessman in Brunford) farewell dinner at Bull and Butcher; says Kaiser will rule England; struck on jaw by brawny Englishman (incident footnote [1] says true).
- Winter; Elijah Butterworth (three sons in army) challenges Tom. Tom stays out.
- New Year: recruiting meeting at Mechanics' Institute (speaker who'd been to Belgium). Tom shouts "By God, I can't stand this!" then "No! By God, no!" and walks to platform: enlists. Polly had a dance that night. Mother: "Lancaster asylum" quip.

### Ch III (Loyal North Lancashires)
- Tom at Thorn and Thistle with Polly at midnight; "I shall be off to-morrow"; Polly: "Of course I'll be true to you."
- Morning: Alice meets Tom at Town Hall: "splendid of you"; mentions a young parson courting her (Tom teases).
- Trained at a Lancashire town ~30 miles away; drunk and disorderly; colonel punishes ("Make a beast of yourself?"); colonel points to Y.M.C.A.
- Robert Penrose (Cornish, public school, Charterhouse 5 yrs, gentleman ranker, refused commission at this stage, later gazetted lieutenant in Surrey). Penrose brings Tom to Y.M.C.A.; Tom learns French ("Je suis, vous etes, nous sommes, ils sont").
- Alec McPhail (Scotch, Black Watch, Presbyterian background, U.P. Kirk elder father, godly mother, drinks whisky, read Ingersoll). Tom and Alec friends.
- Leave: visits Polly; she wants him to drink beer; Tom gives in. Polly's loud dress/feathers.
- Battalion goes to Surrey camp (near Godalming, Charterhouse visible), 11 hundred men; Tom meets Waterman there as lieutenant ("Yes, Mr. Waterman").

### Ch IV (Surrey camp, then France)
- Y.M.C.A. huts; Tom's French report; Mrs Pollard letter about Polly (walks with Jim Dixon; "Look at the stock"); "give Polly Powell the sack".
- Alec: whisky, asks God; drunk before embarkation; Tom refuses drink. Farewell meeting speaker: "you need a Captain, a Guide, a Saviour".
- Folkestone, troopship, Boulogne, troop-train; Ypres area; first sight of guns.

### Ch V (Ypres salient, Belgium)
- Sergeant (served ~20 years; 2 wounds; "Wipers"); Cloth Hall & Cathedral destroyed; poison gas; white flag incident (young officer shot); Tom in trenches; Lancashire lad shot (head above sandbags).
- Bayonet charge; wounded German officer shot the young Englishman who gave him water (footnote: true incident).
- Tom's first prayer: "O God!" repeated. Thinks of Alice praying.

### Ch VI (Alice's night)
- Alice refuses Mr. Skelton (young minister, bachelor). Harry Briarfield (partner in father's firm, Sunday school teacher) proposes; she asks for three days. Mother's wistful look. Alice prays: "O God, save him!"

### Ch VII (warning and Alec's death)
- German shouts from trench: attack at six o'clock next morning, 1100 strong. Tom reports to subaltern; Colonel and Major Blundell; Sergeant Ashworth praises Tom. Attack made; Black Watch rescue.
- Tom's conversion: knows God as Father.
- Alec McPhail wounded; Tom visits hospital (town on road to Cassel); Alec gives heart to God; writes to mother (Highlands, Scottish address); Tom sings "Jesu, Lover of my soul"; they recite Psalm 23; Alec dies next day ("It's a' richt").

### Ch VIII (treachery hunt)
- Colonel Blount (Boer War veteran), Major Blundell, General Withers (Divisional HQ). Waterman seen on canal; Tom watches Waterman by Potijze Road corner; Waterman tosses white paper with stone toward German lines and gives signal cry. Tom tackles him; Penrose arrives; Waterman's pistol; Tom crawls into No-man's-Land, fights German for paper, breaks his shoulder (football trick), bullets wound Tom (left arm, right shoulder). Doctor: "miracle". Colonel Blount visits.

### Ch IX (court-martial)
- Waterman admits: "My father and my mother are German"; name spelled with two n's (German); "I have counted the cost"; executed by firing squad at dawn at a wall.

### Ch X (Tom's fame, Dec 1914 leave)
- Newspapers: "Heroism of a Lancashire Lad"; recommended for D.C.M. Colonel: "as a Lancashire man, I'm proud of you."
- Home leave Dec (Saturday); crowds at station; Polly Powell at station—Tom rejects her ("I don't want to play gooseberry"; "turned teetotaler" follows "the King"). Tom to Mother and Father; family prayer kneeling together.

### Ch XI (Alice reunion; return)
- Sunday church (Alice there, not Harry); Tom: "How are you, Alice?"; walk home; Alice never engaged to Harry Briarfield or the parson; reconciliation; Tom: "I'm only a poor Tommy with a bob a day, will you wait?" Alice: "I can't help waiting for you."
- George Lister approves; Alice goes to Waterloo with Tom; Kipling "ship that found herself" book reference; "au revoir"; narrator saw him off at Waterloo.
- Ends: "Will he come back again...? ... he with a great host of others will fight on... victory which means peace."

---

## BOOK 2 of 2: THE TOP OF THE WORLD (Ethel M. Dell, 1920; Gutenberg 12360)
Dedication to mother; poem prologue ("Nay, I mount only by faith and love / And God's goodness to my soul"; "one I love / Who has promised to wait for me").

Contents: PART I (Ch I–XII: Advice, New Mistress, Whip-Hand, Victory, Miracle, Land of Strangers, Wrong Turning, Comrade, Arrival, Dream, Cross-Roads, Stake); PART II (Comrades, Visitors, Bargain, Capture, Good Cause, Return, Guest, Interruption, Abyss, Desire to Live, Remedy); PART III (New Era, Into Battle, Seed, Mirage, Everybody's Friend, Hero, Net, Summons, For the Sake of the Old Love, Bearer of Evil Tidings, Sharp Corner, Cost); PART IV (Sand of the Desert, Skeleton Tree, Punishment, Evil Thing, Land of Blasted Hopes, Parting, Piet Vreiboom, Out of the Depths, Meeting, Truth, Storm, Sacrifice, By Faith and Love).

### Part I
- Sylvia Ingleton (~23, red-brown eyes, tawny hair), old Jeffcott (head gardener) advises marriage. Father Gilbert Ingleton, squire of the Manor; mother died 3 years earlier. Guy Ranger (son of old Ranger, bailiff; public-school educated; 7 yrs older) loved Sylvia five years ago when she was 18; banished to South Africa farming with cousin (Burke) to prove himself. Squire found another bailiff (dour Scotchman). Sylvia to inherit money at 25.
- Squire marries Mrs. Caroline Emmott (widow; tall, handsome, domineering; "Mrs. Ingleton"; "Madam" name demanded/adopted). Preston (George Preston, M.F.H., rich, Turf money, "Captain Preston", horsey, loud, wants Sylvia) allied with Mrs. Ingleton. Mrs. Ingleton: "whip-hand." Squire gives Mrs. I free hand. 
- Hunt Ball: Sylvia sees no Guy letters for 6 weeks; Preston pressures; Sylvia promises to marry Preston if no word from Guy; Vernon Eversley friendly boy.
- Mrs. Ingleton had Guy's letters stolen/held back. Sylvia confronts; announces leaving; Squire lets her go (asserts himself against wife). Sylvia to Guy in South Africa.
- Ritzen station: man she takes for Guy is Burke Ranger (Guy's cousin, "Burke"), tall? broad, grey eyes, keen; tells her Guy is in delirium tremens; Guy at Blue Hill Farm (20 miles from Ritzen, across Ritter Spruit). Burke: "go back and marry someone else."
- Burke takes her by cart; Ritter Spruit crossed; storm; she's hurt knee; Mary Ann (old Kaffir woman, hideous, lame); Joe (house boy), Fair Rosamond (Rose, lazy), Piet Vreiboom (neighbour, Boer, leering; Burke says she's his wife). Sylvia's dream: Burke and Guy collide on a ledge; Burke galloping; Guy falls down ravine (ambiguous).
- Burke proposes marriage "on pure comrade basis" (Sylvia: "we'll be pals"; "partner"); civil marriage at Brennerstadt; wedding ride to skeleton tree (blasted tree); Burke carves "Fide et Amore" on tree trunk ("commemorating the occasion").
- Guy's cabin on sand by dry watercourse near kopje; padlocked.

### Part II
- Merstons (Bill Merston, cheerful, red-faced; Matilda Merston, pinched, bitter; six children died; "Garden of Eden"). Mrs Merston says Burke sjamboked cousin Guy out.
- Burke: "You've raised Cain." Sylvia asks to find Guy; Burke agrees ("On one condition... play a straight game"). Guy is tending bar at Hoffstein's in Brennerstadt (miner saloon); Kelly (Donovan Kelly, Irish manager of diamond mine, rubicund, "my son") helps. Kelly and Burke fetch Guy by force.
- Guy confesses; Burke pins him down; Guy wounds Burke's chin with glass; sober, calmer.
- Burke rescues Guy; prepares hut ("guest-hut") for him; Sylvia unrelenting; Guy shoots himself at door (revolver, "boss shot"), Kieff (Dr. Saul Kieff, Jewish, onyx eyes, "raven", morphine remedy) attends.
- Guy reveals drug use; Burke "pulls her up"; Sylvia loves Guy.

### Part III
- Kieff gives Sylvia morphia; Burke furious; Burke dismisses Kieff ("helped him on his way"). Guy recovers. Burke's attempt to kiss; Sylvia's "the kiss of peace"; Burke later assaults? (he asserts rights; she defies).
- Veldt fire at Vreiboom's; Burke trapped; Guy saves Burke. Guy: "You are mine." Sylvia to Mrs Merston. Burke's strong-box key; Guy takes money. Guy's wins Wilbraham diamond (raffle). Kelly, Kieff.
- Guy tells Sylvia: "I married him because he was so like you" (her answer). Guy's suicidal fallout; Sylvia kisses him.

### Part IV
- Brennerstadt: Guy's hut burns/flood; Burke tries to kill Guy; Sylvia pleads; Burke's hut; Guy dies in flood ("Fide et Amore" carved). Diamond sold; Burke & Sylvia reunited ("By faith and love"); Mrs Merston reconciled; Guy's dying words; Kieff dies (opium, Brennerstadt; Burke thrashed him publicly); Sylvia and Burke go "to the top of the world."

Ending: Burke: "I love you with my whole soul"; Sylvia: "I wanted you to tell me that?"; "nearer to the stars... than to the world at their feet."

---

Key recurring phrases: "top of the world"; "by faith and love"; "land of strangers"; "partner"; "Fide et Amore"; "Cherry-ripe" (Preston's nickname for Sylvia); "Diamond" (Sylvia's horse); "Joe", "Mary Ann", "Rose/Fair Rosamond"; "Hans Schafen" (Dutch overseer, rubber-soled boots).
